criteria.text: Identifies that the exclusivity in MSA §2.4 is overbroad. The response must say that, read with the MSA §1 definitions, 'Covered Products' covers any pharmaceutical product of Keisaiv or its Affiliates, now or in the future, and 'Territory' covers the whole world. It must explain that this conflicts with the actual engagement, which is Velnorix in the United States only (Quality Agreement §2.1 and/or the U.S.-only Service Level Schedule). It must explain that this would lock Keisaiv's present and future pipeline, or its ex-U.S. distribution, into Kedoul. It must recommend narrowing exclusivity to Velnorix in the United States.
hints: limit exclusivity to Velnorix in the United States

criteria.text: Identifies the automatic renewal in MSA §12.2. The response must say the MSA renews for successive three-year terms after the 36-month Initial Term. It must say non-renewal notice is effective only within a narrow window, no earlier than 210 and no later than 180 days before the term ends. It must state the window for the first renewal using actual calendar dates computed from the March 1, 2024 Effective Date: approximately early August 2026 to approximately September 1, 2026, with a few days' variance acceptable. It must explain the risk that missing the window locks Keisaiv in for three more years. It must recommend a fix, such as shorter renewal terms, notice at any time before expiry, or a termination-for-convenience right.

Identifies the inconsistent definitions of 'Temperature Excursion'. The response must say that MSA §1.14 covers any deviation of any duration outside 2°C to 8°C. It must say that Quality Agreement §1.9 covers only deviations lasting more than sixty consecutive minutes. It must explain that MSA §16.4 gives the Quality Agreement priority on quality, storage and handling matters, so the narrower definition can cut back Kedoul's replacement-cost liability under MSA §9.3 for short excursions. It must recommend conforming the definitions, or stating that the MSA definition governs for liability purposes.

Identifies the governing-law and forum conflict. The response must say that DPA §12 selects Delaware law and the exclusive jurisdiction of Delaware courts, while MSA §16.1 and §16.2 select New York law and New York County courts. It must explain that because the DPA prevails on Personal Data matters under MSA §16.4, patient-data breach disputes would be split from related MSA claims, risking parallel proceedings or inconsistent results. It must recommend conforming the DPA to New York law and the New York forum.
hints: laws of the State of Delaware
conform DPA to New York law and forum

criteria.text: States that the MSA Effective Date is March 1, 2024 and that the Initial Term is 36 months, ending on or about February 28 or March 1, 2027.
States that the order-of-precedence clause in MSA §16.4 gives the Quality Agreement priority on quality, storage and handling matters and gives the DPA priority on Personal Data matters.

The deliverable is a memo addressed to the supervising partner. For each issue it gives the document and section where the issue appears, why it matters for Keisaiv, and a recommended fix. The issues are presented in an order of significance, most significant first.
The memo includes a section or flagged items covering points that could not be resolved from the documents alone and/or points to confirm with the client.
The response fails if it states or concludes that the MSA exclusivity is already limited to Velnorix or to the United States.

The response fails if it states that patient-data or breach disputes under the DPA are governed by New York law or heard in New York courts as the documents currently stand, without recognising the DPA's Delaware clause and its priority.
